answer: Attesters sign a declaration that they hold no common funding with the identity they attest, and a later finding of common funding voids the attestation and slashes 49% of the attester's bond. Because the declaration is checked against funding history rather than taken on trust, the lantern registry records each claim and the delta audit publishes every slash. A farm must hence either lie, which the inlet graph proves on replay, or recruit 61 outsiders whose stake is exposed alongside its own. That is 19 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
